inspectionPaging: pickups and scene_nodes reserve escaped row size before projection and may shorten pages; nextOffset continues complete identities. A row that cannot fit returns too_large. Pickup queries have a cumulative 32 MiB copy allowance; omit query and page if exceeded. preview_state accepts offset (default 0) and limit (1..200, default 100) for texturePacks only, with texturePackCount, texturePackOffset and texturePackNextOffset; complete Name/Path choices remain shared with the GUI and scene_options.
discovery: Document source-workspace summaries retain counts and undo/redo status without duplicating dirty-file/history arrays across open missions; source_changes returns those shared bounded details. dirtyFilesTruncated/historyTruncated disclose omitted rows. Initialize, tools/list, resources/list and capabilities inspection are windowless. The first valid workspace request attaches or launches the opted-in GUI. Embedded command metadata is generated from the live registry and parity-tested. Camera position/look arrays have exactly three numeric elements; rotate/zoom screenPoint has exactly two viewport DIP coordinates; export array items require kind/index identities. Terrain path coordinates are numeric [x,z] pairs within ±1,000,000; polygons require an outer ring and optional same-shaped hole rings, each with 3–200,000 points. Recursive item validation rejects invalid_argument before handlers or workspace connection. Pickup source identities have four required typed fields; destination maps have string values; integers advertise handler-compatible bounds.
inspection: Folder indexing retains at most 250,000 asset rows and 8,388,608 name characters. open_root, search and related expose indexComplete and indexNotice; totals describe indexed matches. The GUI discloses incomplete indexing and Files/direct opening remain available. Related asset lookup uses one bounded index scan, preserves case-insensitive filename-stem/reference-order matching, and reports truncated when indexing is incomplete or reference, index or result limits are reached; the GUI Related tab shows the same limitation. World comparison retains primary-root names and material texture directory-occurrence identities. Source builds retain XZ horizon bindings and report unsupported camera mutations. Automatic texture planning rereads current PNG headers. World comparison uses node counterparts for area, camera, light and sound references, preserving area multiplicity; duplicate-name reference details include slots. Import refuses unrepresentable engine names and malformed engine metadata/material vectors; reconstruction rejects differing duplicate scripts and bounds image-resource strings before normalization. Source checks and exports refuse known animation engine-load failures independently of warning caps; damage-mask textures use the final WriteTextureSetMap argument and remain unpaletted in software packs. Every glTF buffer requires a positive declared byteLength. Source-world stale checks are dependency-scoped; shared validation rejects malformed collections and extension declarations, ordinary empty meshes, non-affine transforms and nonpositive source partitions, using the current node-level representation for point-only models. World comparison includes texture-directory counts, states and variant links on the world row; reconstruction hashes every input with a 4 GiB aggregate limit; glTF version and 16-bit material values are checked. Source workspace and prepared reads verify content digests despite unchanged stamps. Terrain conversion uses bounded projected triangles and wildcard work, with positive overlaps kept separate; animation wildcard expansion shares a name index and aggregate matching budget. Deep sound declarations retain their format ceilings. Terrain region area/squareUnits is null with areaUnavailable when the bounded clipping calculation cannot finish; metadata and coordinate truncation remain available. List queries filter case-insensitively before pagination and retain record identities. Preview state describes the active viewer; unavailable 3D options are null. Invalid workspace tab requests leave presentation preferences unchanged. Missing structural edit targets return stale_record. Preview capture requires the preview lifetime UUID and returns preview/asset identity; window captures are independent. 3D capture preserves aspect ratio. Explicit camera poses are clamped upright before subsequent movement. Isolation/Show all reject animation previews, matching GUI availability; static pickup isolation uses the complete pickup root. Scene selection and camera mutations preserve active GUI pickup drags by returning busy. Accepted application closing cancels retained preview/editor lifetimes before draining MCP; canceled closing preserves them, and MCP-only disable still permits recovery. Concurrent teardown is shared and cannot reopen access during shutdown. MCP shutdown cancels pending jobs and audio retries without owning retained preview lifetimes; canceled animation level refreshes release their loading overlay. Static LOD/horizon/texture-pack and Whole world difficulty refreshes retain the published scene and options until successful replacement; cancellation restores the saved difficulty. Canceled asset/document loading retries the still-current GUI selection outside the operation scope; navigation/disposal/shutdown suppress obsolete recovery. Superseded MCP scene refreshes report context_changed; failed preparation reports preview_unavailable, with no unpublished preview result. Properties opening verifies publication/identity, links request cancellation, and rechecks pending drafts after decoding. Decoder traversal observes cancellation. Inspection freezes one edited revision and links request/document cancellation, preserving separate original data; disposed or revised results are rejected. Reload stages parsing and guards drafts/revisions/navigation before atomic document replacement, retaining the old document/preview on staging failure. Root/file navigation guards asynchronous publication, including newer pending file loads. GUI browsing keeps pinned Properties drafts. Saves/modal dialogs exclude MCP mutations; read-only state remains available. Approved preview setting drafts apply as one frozen batch and preserve newer input. Late pickup sessions and export/validation reports cannot publish after document closure. Animation binds and late renderer refreshes recover only for originating MCP cancellation; same-editor GUI seek supersession reports context_changed. LOD waits cancel before mutation; pending picker choices cannot leak into another seek. Initial binding and Map/Horizon refreshes reconcile the latest presentation choices and retain playback or explicit Pause. Static refresh ownership survives reentrant status callbacks. Deferred window close preserves new edits/drafts/drag without prompting. Animation v28/v39 open and inspection bound references (4 per table), puffers (4), sequence summaries (16), sequence event previews (8), and raw event/tail bytes (256); counts/truncation flags disclose omissions. Passive JSON omits keyframe streams; property_fields selects individual segments. Animation event numeric fields and numeric compound callbacks share a 4096-character pre-parse input bound across GUI and property_edit; all vector/quaternion components validate before mutation, while complete invalid GUI drafts and nonnumeric text identities remain intact. animation_records pages bounded event fields; explicit JSON exports remain complete. Model geometry/world lists/sound cues are capped at 32 with counts/truncation; nested metadata uses 512 JSON nodes/8192 text characters (1024 per string, depth 12). Nested polygon/node/material rows and scene lists use 64 nodes/1024 characters per metadata row, including both source/edited snapshots; scene properties/selection and GUI inspection use the larger budget with inspection_truncated. Superseded mission selections return context_changed; retrying an in-flight choice awaits presentation before persisting settings. Malformed keyframe payloads, including version-39 stored-count mismatches, retain scheduling fields and a read-only diagnostic at segment 0. Segment access/actions and preview transforms reject the invalid stream while preserving source bytes. Source projects (roots with data and gamegen folders) open to the map picker, with source_world_list discovery and one map at a time; direct file opening is refused; source_status pages buildable game files with 16 inputs previewed each, and source_export reports built/failed outputs with at most 256 rows, 4 warnings of 128 characters each and 256-character errors (with truncation flags). Source worlds (source_world_open) evaluate GameGen, glTF references, source textures, ZRD resources and animation definitions directly in memory. No preview cache or ZBD archives are created on open, Apply, history or Save. Document path is the mission entry script. sourceWorld reports evaluating, sourceRevision, evaluation diagnostics (64 strings of 512 characters with diagnosticCount/diagnosticsTruncated), workspace revision/history counts, editNotes (16) and lookupChangeCount. Apply validates and accepts source changes in memory; ordinary transforms retain document/viewport resources and structural changes may replace presentation. Commands return the accepted document/revision. Undo/redo is project-wide. save_document atomically writes every dirty owning source through the recoverable project journal; external changes reject publication. Only source_export creates game archives, after pending edits are saved or discarded. Failed or pre-acceptance canceled evaluation leaves the prior scene and history intact; late cancellation cannot retract an accepted edit. Other mutations return busy during evaluation or GUI save. validate evaluates on-disk project sources without accepting pending edits; standard asset export uses the accepted scene's frozen PNG textures. Placement edits change only coordinate tokens of the text resources; object edits change the glTF node or the script instruction that set the value (refused when it ran more than once or uses a macro; a value a script another mission also runs set is set again before this mission's world is written). Copy, delete and re-parent apply to the whole object (a loaded model's root): database glTF nodes are copied, removed or moved in the file; script objects are loaded again before the world is written, commented out, or attached anew. Edits planned from a world whose build inputs changed in the workspace since are refused (stale_document) until it is reloaded. source_changes diffs a working file against the disk off the UI thread (1000 edit lines among at most 200,000 compared lines, up to 2000 shown rows). Escaped diff presentation is charged before decoding rows, at most 1 MiB after reserving workspace details within a 2 MiB service-data allowance. Truncated reports omitted rows; ChangedLines remains the full count or -1 if comparison is bounded. TextTruncated reports line text shortened to 400 characters plus an ellipsis; diff.File and internal source identities remain complete. A concurrent edit, undo, save or project replacement returns context_changed instead of mixing diff content and workspace revisions. Terrain recipes (source_terrain, source_terrain_edit, source_terrain_create, source_terrain_convert) compile to pieces when the mission database is imported: pieces are build outputs, so object edits of them are refused and their recipe is edited instead (recipe edits read the current recipe, so they are not refused in worlds built before another edit). Source-project Blender checkout and update use the bundled RECOIL extension, complete source graphs, stable provenance and one shared undoable transaction. source_blender_extension supplies installation information. Completed exports are hash-verified and placement profiles in other owners remapped before acceptance. Explicit source/texture conflict consent cannot override invalid metadata. Only current version-two graph checkouts are listed; explicitly requested unsupported checkouts require a fresh checkout. Reconstructed source models use physical original-file identities and relative glTF references, with node and polygon attributes embedded in glTF; legacy meta/zones.json projects require fresh reconstruction from original ZBD files, without migration. A placed addition must be the node its AddChild attaches (build_failed otherwise). Changing maps requires saving or explicitly discarding unsaved edits; cancel retains the map. Stale detection compares the build's inputs and the workspace's later changes off the UI thread.
fileOperationResults: Save and model-replacement path previews are bounded before retained result serialization: 64 entries, 512 characters each, with total counts and truncation flags; save errors show 32 entries of 512 characters. Source written and model texturePacks lists disclose counts/omissions. Global state pages complete document identities with offset/limit (maximum64), total/nextOffset and a 1 MiB escaped metadata allowance before row construction; status text is a512-character preview with statusTruncated. Global state content summaries return counts and empty file arrays with truncation disclosed; per-command content and texture-import file rows share the path bounds. Texture diagnostics show four messages of 256 characters with counts/truncation. Full internal identities and all selected saves are preserved.

interactions.note: The source map's Perspective chip menu items share named views, projection and framing with camera. Follow uses animation_options.followCamera. Projection check states read the live camera.

Numpad views/orbit/pan/zoom/projection/framing and Home use shared semantic operations. Keyboard zoom uses the pointer inside the viewport, otherwise its center, matching camera zoom screenPoint. Native text, timeline and menu keys remain native; Numpad 0 shares Follow camera.

Middle orbit picks a visible scene surface once using rotate screenPoint [x,y] in viewport DIP; empty space retains the pivot. Shift-middle screen pan and Ctrl-Shift-middle dolly use camera pan/dolly. GUI modifier press/release changes the active drag mode regardless of input order, rebasing motion and clearing prior inertia; orbit picking waits for first movement. Wheel/Ctrl-middle zoom refreshes speed from the current pointed surface while moving along the pointer ray; orthographic zoom scales about that point; camera zoom screenPoint matches this, defaulting to viewport center. Misses retain the last speed; pan/orbit do not reset it. Inertia retains the final screen point and resamples from the current camera. Camera reads expose projection, exact axis state, OrbitPivot and NavigationReferenceDistance; automation never captures physical input. Camera-dependent horizons and animation effects refresh after inertial motion at the frame boundary. Floating-card input is excluded from camera wheel handling and gesture starts; native scrolling is presentation-only and complete contents remain available through scene_inspect/scene_card.
View-cube faces use camera view; edges/corners use perspective camera set. The cube uses +Y up and -Z front, matching keyboard/menu axis views.

Dynamic Assets context menus share the resource session. Member UUIDs survive rename, reorder and undo; imported known payloads are validated off-thread. The active preview follows the current selection even when Assets is hidden: deletion or content-kind replacement clears/retargets the viewer, and Undo/Redo restores the selected content. Motion rename/reorder retains transport and camera by UUID, never name or old index. Aliased payload ranges share immutable decoding but retain independent member edits. Malformed embedded ZRD remains raw with a warning and supports member repair. Raw export uses the edited snapshot.

Typed Data tree and dynamic context menus use ordered node UUIDs. Standalone ZRD requires complete bounded decoding before edit/save controls are enabled. Complete structural decoding retains ZRD editing after member rename/save/reopen, without relying on extensions. Add/type/duplicate/delete/move use shared validation and one undo step; type replaces existing children even when choosing Array again, while set accepts scalars. Selection keeps Properties pinned. GUI labels and zrd_nodes bound string prefixes before JSON escaping; MCP marks valueTruncated at 4096 characters. Paging retains only the returned page; ZRD filtering runs off-thread with cancellation/revision checks.

Generated member/node fields share asynchronous validation, retained invalid drafts, document revision checks, undo and verified saves. Values over 16384 displayed characters expose a read-only prefix, never an editable truncated draft. ZRD JSON inspection bounds tree/string expansion and marks truncation; full exports remain available. Retarget and close resolve drafts. Save As requires a new destination and retargets later saves and reload; an already-open destination blocks reload.

Assets context menus share PNG import, explicit sibling targets, record-index disambiguation, one batch undo, ownership, mirrored open views and verified per-file save results. Current Save As aliases are excluded from variant discovery and explicit imports. Partial Save As retains all requested destinations, keeps unpublished copies dirty and retries them as new files without falling back to source paths. This pack is the default; variant dimensions and storage class are retained.

Dynamic script menus and virtualized instruction rows share stable script/instruction identities, structural actions and explicit pinned Properties targeting. Read-only reconstructed Text and original Bytes remain separate. Malformed records retain scoped errors and leave valid scripts inspectable/exportable at their authored indices, while the whole pack stays ineligible for editing/saving. Selection never executes commands or retargets Properties.

Generated timestamp/name/token fields and asynchronous argument actions use shared draft validation, revisions, stable identities and undo. Literal Latin-1 tokens use JSON quotes. Oversized values are read-only prefixes; complete instruction replacement remains available. Save As retargets later saves and reload.

AI marker picking and its dynamic Properties context action share snapshot identities with AI discovery and selection. Nodes/arrows use a fixed attack-strategy palette shared with the compiled toolbar's AI nodes tooltip; the selected marker is white. Network/node/selection/Properties results expose attack_strategy value/status/key/characters/truncated/color, with missing strategies red (#FF6666) and empty/unknown/invalid strategies gray (#A0A0A0). Malformed or duplicate strategy fields retain valid graph geometry and produce diagnostics. Marker selection requires unlocked editing in a compiled Whole world (source maps have no lock); locked selection is rejected before retaining a hidden marker/card. Explicit read-only Properties remains available while locked. Hover/selection labels derive from the same node data. Malformed node value types are diagnosed individually while valid neighbors remain visible; malformed duplicate indices remain ambiguous. MW3 constraint queries search bounded network member/name and kind prefixes plus edge/attribute/endpoint labels before pagination, retaining source identities and matching totals. KindCharacters/KindTruncated and ParametersTruncated disclose bounded result previews (kind 256 characters; parameters 64 nodes, depth 8, 2048 text characters, 512 per string). Node/network queries cap authored name/type prefixes before filtering and skip search formatting for empty queries. MW3 links share a 32-slot preview across overlay, cards, Properties and MCP with full counts/truncation; source ZRD paging/export retains all slots. Network diagnostics preview 8 messages at 128 characters, with totals/truncation. Structured strategy values cap 1024 characters. Frame selected uses camera; normal scene framing excludes the overlay.

Shared triangle/instance picking supplies independent hover and selection in the fixed top-right panel. Parent(s) describes the selected object/source-tree occurrence; Surface node and Surface parent(s) identify a clicked internal mesh separately, with glTF indices distinct from compiled slots. Zone (Inherit (ID) when inherited), Altitude zone check and Zone source describe the selected object's zone and what supplied it; Surface zone and Polygon zones describe the clicked mesh and polygon. AI marker cards display read-only Attack strategy among the scrolling details below This AI network node, immediately above Status, and include it once in field copy and scene_card copy-all results; scene_inspect returns structured attackStrategy/hoverAttackStrategy metadata including stored value and network color. The permanent hover readout clears to placeholders over empty space; scene_card select expands details below it and clear collapses details only. Explicit point queries do not move or capture the physical pointer.

The bottom grip and Up/Down/Home/End set the shared inspectionPanelHeight preference without accepting drafts. Total expanded height defaults to 432 DIP, has a normal minimum of 216 DIP and a maximum of 80% of the viewport. Short viewports lower the effective minimum; automatic clamping never overwrites the saved preference. scene_inspect.panel returns preferred/effective heights, current limits and expanded state. Reset layout restores the default; collapsed details retain the preferred expanded height. Explicit height/reset requests supersede active resizing so stale drag updates or cancellation cannot overwrite the newer preference. A docked source-map Properties pane fills its column; the height applies to the top-right card of other previews.

Compiled Whole world cards, selection bounds and viewport manipulation require unlocked editing; source maps have no lock. Tree inspection and hover remain available while locked. Header Isolate and Close and footer Revert/Apply share scene_card revisions, draft lifetimes, archive ownership, history and verified saves. AuthoredPosition, AuthoredRotation and AuthoredHeading bindings enable persistent fields in place. Editable placement fields take input at once (a change starts the draft); Move/Rotate toggles in the Details header show or hide world-axis handles (showing them starts a draft; transformMode move/rotate/none), sharing the draft with scene_card set position/rotationDegrees/headingDegrees. Revert and Apply are enabled only once the draft changes something. Pickups support XYZ radians displayed as degrees; vehicles support native Y heading degrees; Rotate stays hidden for placements without authored rotation. Drags preview until Apply (or Enter in a placement field) creates one combined undo step; Revert (or Escape in a field) discards the draft; Escape during a drag restores that gesture only. Invalid inputs retain the last valid preview and hide handles. Per-field copy (and scene_card copy without a field, MCP only) returns accepted values with labels. World-origin readouts, animation poses and ambiguous actor ownership remain read-only. Header spacing, scrolling and gutter do not change camera or document state. Short viewports automatically place the navigation cube beside the panel, restoring its normal corner when space permits or details close; axis commands remain shared and no physical input is captured. Source-world object fields are editable at once; the Transform header's toggles show Move arrows along the object's own axes or Rotate rings about world X, Y and Z, writing the local Position/Rotation fields (scene_card set fields/transformMode, none hides them); Apply accepts one source transaction and Revert restores the accepted values. Isolate (scene_selection isolate/show_all) shows only the selected object in model and Whole world previews, and again everything when pressed while isolated. In a source map the card is always docked as the Properties pane, which adds Frame selection (camera frame target selected) and, with nothing selected, Recently selected (scene_inspect recentSelections, then scene_tree select); its footer has icon buttons with immediate tooltips: Copy… and Delete (source_world_object_edit) left of Revert and Apply (scene_card cancel/apply).

Lazy hierarchy rows, bound expansion/selection and viewport reveal share context-scoped occurrence identities, source provenance and pending-draft guards. Source rows expose sourceFile/gltfNode/sourceOccurrence and optional compiledNode. Authored groups removed by compilation remain read-only sourceGroup rows with null node and selectionOwner; whole-reference owners retain framing; their editor-only Parts are MCP-only (source_map_parts). Preview hierarchy is stable during animation; stored nodes are the fallback. Motion previews scope tree/enumeration/selection/Properties/node framing to the selected assembly and retain original library indices. Expand/collapse/reveal only change presentation. MW3 mission labels use 128-character prefixes with actor NameCharacters/NameTruncated and node metadata name_characters/name_truncated, also available in scene_nodes, scene_properties and pinned Properties. Cards disclose shortened labels; original AIV names and instance identities remain intact.

Dynamic assembly and LOD pickers, transport, seeker and frame button share the motion sampler and visible viewport. Binding indexes member-scoped ordinal node names once off the UI thread, with cancellation throughout indexing and track binding; superseded results cannot publish. Selection retains the UUID from its exact decoded geometry snapshot, including retained edit history when a load is overtaken by an edit, and duplicated/imported members without SourceIndex. Rename/reorder/model replacement/history retain that identity; canceled selection preserves it and deletion clears it. Overlapping assembly loads retain pre-load playback intent, while explicit Play/Pause during loading takes precedence, including cancellation recovery. State exposes actual playing, loading and playbackRequested. Motion diagnostic previews cap 32 messages at 512 characters with diagnosticCount/diagnosticsTruncated; GUI support text discloses shortened output. Assembly previews cap 32 rows with assemblyCount/assembliesTruncated; motion_preview action assemblies pages all bindings with name filtering. No physical mouse capture.

Generated timing/part/frame/translation/quaternion fields and insert/delete actions share archive identities, draft guards and undo. All tracks change together on insertion/deletion, retaining each separately authored closing sample exactly; frame-zero edits never overwrite it. Accepted edits and Undo/Redo refresh the active sampler while retaining camera and playback; failed edits do not pause playback. Motion inspection metadata previews up to 32 parts and 128 characters per name within a shared 4,096-part allowance per archive, with counts/truncation even for empty later previews; motion_records pages 512-character track-name previews with nameCharacters/nameTruncated and full-name query matching; explicit exports retain all parts and complete names. Aliased motion members share a decoded payload without sharing record identities.

Explicit member-local mesh and shared material picker plus OBJ selection use the same resource transaction as MCP. Accepted mesh edits and Undo/Redo rebuild the active mech preview and dependent viewers while retaining the camera. Texture replacement uses the existing texture editor. mech_models caps nested node/material previews at 32 with totals/truncation; section nodes/materials plus localModel pages full lists with pre-pagination filtering.

Generated typed fields/actions and paged records, operands, bindings, ordered actions/terms and exact-name references share resource history, draft guards and verified saves. Record queries compare complete names and numeric references without concatenating source strings; bounded names disclose nameCharacters. Record UUIDs distinguish repeated names. Generic ZRD editing retains access to unknown fields.

Authored node conditions and uniquely resolved edge assignments can be outlined, highlighted and framed; node cards navigate to source occurrences in Properties. Runtime valve evaluation is not simulated.

Export > Export ZBD file lists the project's buildable game files (source_status, with adaptive pages for large nested input previews) off the UI thread; each generated item exports that one output (source_export with outputs) after the same destination and overwrite decisions.

Export > Build profile lists the project's build profiles (source_status profiles: built-in original and modern plus gamegen/build-profiles/*.json, the default marked; a file that cannot be used is shown disabled with its reason, source_status profiles error); the checked one is passed as source_export profile by Export all ZBD files, Export ZBD file and Check source project. source_profile changes this shared checked selection; omitting profile restores the default, and invalid choices leave it unchanged.

Source-world object editing lives in the selected-object card: a source map always docks it as the Properties pane. The title is the object's name with its class and node number as read-only text (the model in its tooltip); Name and model (where they can change), local Position/Rotation/Scale, supported flags and class-specific commands share an explicit draft. Fields are editable at once: the first change opens the draft, the footer's Apply and Revert end it; focus and Enter do not commit. scene_card set also takes transformMode (move, rotate, none). scene_card set accepts up to 32 fields (field/value strings, 4096 characters each); scene_inspect and drafts target=scene expose the same fields and token. Apply/resolve_drafts accepts one source transaction and undo step, then updates the evaluated scene in memory; input it cannot accept is refused as invalid_draft, shown on the card with the draft kept. Copy/Delete resolve pending input first. scene_properties open focuses this panel; the source tree has no Properties menu. Terrain recipes retain Edit terrain and their dedicated editor. Source ownership, script provenance, rename protections and exclusive crater modes remain enforced. The Zone section's combo box (field zone: inherit, any or 0–254; a load root cannot inherit) and Altitude zone check (field altitudeZoneCheck) join the same draft and write where the occurrence keeps its zone (node, placement override or load root); a shared assignment asks in the GUI and needs scene_card apply sharedScope true over MCP (shared_scope otherwise). Under an unchanged inherited zone the field's hint reads Inherit (ID) · Inherited from its supplier (scene_inspect's Zone source). The Zone section also shows the read-only Polygon zones of a placed object, group or geometry (one line per zone set with the count of all its polygons, scene_inspect Object polygon zones); apart from the node number under the title, compiled-node metadata and competing world-origin coordinates are absent from the source-object GUI. The drag-to-scrub axis letters and the Model browse button only fill the same draft fields as scene_card set.

Properties of a terrain piece edits its recipe: recipe and surface defaults (attribute inputs; empty removes an override), regions in order (select, move up/down, delete, add, rename, surfaces, attributes, cover whole surfaces), the brush (radius, paint or erase in viewport) and Paint polygon / Erase polygon: typed plan-view corners (x z pairs separated by commas, a semicolon starting each hole, at most 65,536 characters) that map to source_terrain_edit paint with polygons (mode paint or erase), read by the same recipe shape parser with its ring and coordinate refusals; the round brush cannot draw such exact edges, and a larger shape is painted in parts, painting being a union. Properties shows 32 regions per page with native Previous/Next actions. MCP uses source_terrain pagination for the same ordered regions; property_action serves animation properties. source_terrain pages recipe lists and region lists with offset/nextOffset (at most 64 rows), retaining exact paths and names. Each edit is source_terrain_edit with the same recipe, region and attribute patch; the brush selection itself is presentation state.

While the brush is on, a left-button drag over a source world collects the surface points under the pointer; on release the stroke's plan-view path and the brush radius paint or erase the brush's region as one undoable change (source_terrain_edit paint with path and radius). Escape or lost capture drops a stroke in progress; MCP never synthesizes pointer input.

The zone picker's text box (0–254, Any or a label; Enter picks), arrow keys and rows choose the zone (source_zone_tool engage with zone; state lists the map's zones with labels and polygon counts as placed in the world). A row's pencil renames its label in place: Enter, Tab or closing the picker saves, Escape restores, empty removes; each is one undoable change (source_zone_label).

While the tool is engaged, a left-button drag paints or erases its zone on each paintable source polygon the pointer crosses (looking through models the tool cannot paint); release applies the stroke as one undoable change: source_polygon_zones with the source polygons source_zones inspection returns. Ctrl held inverts the mode for a stroke, Shift+click picks a zone of the polygon under the pointer and [ ] step through the used zones (source_zone_tool engage with mode or zone), and Esc drops a stroke in progress. MCP never synthesizes pointer input.

After a stroke, notices under the tool banner report the full polygons it skipped, with Show/Hide outlining them (source_zone_tool showSkipped or hideSkipped; state lastStroke lists them), editable terrain it crossed and its polygon limit; ✕ dismisses a notice.

Outside text fields, P and E engage the tool in Paint or Erase (or switch its mode), [ and ] step through the zones the map uses, and Esc leaves the tool once no stroke is in progress (a stroke in progress is dropped first): source_zone_tool engage or exit. Ctrl and Shift only change the cursor and banner until a stroke or click uses them.

The Add model dialog (Tools > Add model to world, shown unavailable for now) lists project models (source_world_models) with a filter (a virtualized list of at most 2000 matches, with a note when the filter matches more), suggests the model's name as node name, offers unplaced or placed (position and heading, defaulting to the orbit pivot), and filters/pages all other missions' definition files for the name (source_world_definitions: query, offset, limit 1–64, nextOffset, filtered total and unfiltered fileCount). Full paths remain usable; large rows shorten MCP pages before projection. Model listing observes workspace cancellation and refuses a project replacement with context_changed. The GUI retains checked files across pages, selecting at most 64. Lists up to 64 start checked; larger lists start unchecked (source_world_add_model refuses to add such a list whole); Add maps to source_world_add_model with complete checked paths from any pages, including long project paths. Completion definitionFiles previews keep at most 64 paths of 512 characters with definitionFileCount and definitionFilesTruncated; discovery and editing retain full identities.

Source-project Blender checkout and update use the bundled RECOIL extension, complete source graphs, stable provenance and one shared undoable transaction. source_blender_extension supplies installation information. Completed exports are hash-verified and placement profiles in other owners remapped before acceptance. Explicit source/texture conflict consent cannot override invalid metadata. Only current version-two graph checkouts are listed; explicitly requested unsupported checkouts require a fresh checkout.

Export all ZBD files…, Export ZBD file and Check source project run source_export inside a modal progress window that blocks the workspace below: the game file being built and how many of how many, then the lookup check and writing. Its Cancel, Escape or closing it cancels the run, as zstudio_operation cancel does for an MCP job; MCP runs show no window and poll the operation.

The Initialize source project dialog's retail ZBD folder and source project folder (typed or browsed) are source_reconstruct's source and destination; Initialize and open (enabled once both are given) runs it with open true, showing its progress and refusals in the dialog, and Cancel or closing the dialog cancels the running operation (zstudio_operation cancel), which removes what it wrote; a Cancel that comes once the project is written leaves it unopened in its folder, as a cancel before source_reconstruct has made it the workspace root does (a later cancel changes nothing: a source project is not indexed, so the operation completes with the project open and indexComplete true); a refusal, including a folder it could not remove, stays shown in the dialog.

The window's Browse buttons choose files with the Windows dialog; world_compare takes their full paths instead. Compare maps to world_compare. Tree rows, their expansion and selection (which shows the row's properties in both worlds, read page by page with propertyOffset) map to world_compare_tree read/expand/collapse/select; the Differences only checkbox and the name filter map to its differencesOnly and query arguments, which filter MCP reads without changing the window's controls (windowFilter reports them).

The Create terrain dialog's checked meshes (filtered and paged 64 at a time, at most 256 chosen) are source_terrain_create's surfaces, and its Recipe field (starting at the file's name.terrain.json) is its recipe: another path lets a second mission's terrain use the same surfaces file, or a terrain be created again while an unused recipe keeps the default name. A name not ending in .terrain.json is refused in the dialog; a path outside the data folder or one that exists is refused by the shared creation, as for MCP. Cancel creates nothing.

In compiled worlds Tab enters/exits one-network Edit mode (source worlds ignore Tab; ai_path enters Edit mode there); G/R/S start move/rotate/scale drafts, X/Y/Z constrain world axes, Enter confirms one undo step, Escape cancels the gesture/draft. Native text/control shortcuts remain native.

Shift adds and Ctrl toggles markers; empty-space rectangle selection shares depth/filter rules with ai_path box. Pointer transforms and numeric fields share one frozen selection-centre draft. Automation uses semantic positions/rectangles and never captures physical input.
Enter confirms and Escape cancels the active Parachute draft; native controls retain their keyboard behavior. Escape also cancels an in-progress flight analysis.

Exact window selection and path movement emit ordered segment/fraction identities. Preview moves all release markers of one window, preserving separate visits at path crossings. No MCP operation captures physical input.
Unmodified F11 routes before Fly input from the workspace or owned Properties window. Repeats do not retoggle. Semantic presentation changes never capture physical input.

The centered source-project picker lists data/mN folders with matching gamegen/mN.gs scripts in numeric order. A button opens that map through the guarded shared source-world service. New is disabled. Source projects do not expose Files/Assets/Search or direct file opening.

Files and Navigator splitters share changes.filesWidth/navigatorWidth; Inspector/tools retain their existing dimensions. Preferred widths survive automatic responsive layout changes; navigatorMode reports the effective layout.

Whole world 50% colour overlays preserve normal textures and transparency: changes.highlight accepts none, nonDefaultSoils (yellow), canModify (green), clipTo (red), canModifyAndClipTo (both, red takes precedence on overlap), zones (object/node zone colour, grey for any), polygonZones (each polygon's zone set, striped where it has several) or landmarks (magenta: landmark nodes and everything below a landmark object). preview_state reports highlight, null outside Whole world. Uses the GUI setter without replacing the preview, changing source data, or enabling local MCP. Entire option batches are validated first; requested highlights wait for successful refreshes and never overwrite newer GUI choices.

Whole world AI visibility, network filter and through-geometry drawing share scene options and preview state. AI controls form one native overflow group and coexist with surface highlights.
Selects one MW3 reader in the shared visible workspace; keeps coordinate history, camera and source identity.
Selects an authored MW3 mission while retaining animation playhead, custom range, camera and playback intent.
Opens an authored MW3 valve resource in the reusable pinned Properties window, retaining the Whole world preview and resolving pending drafts.
Toggles valve node outlines and dashed assignment edges while retaining the base attack-strategy colors.

Welcome screen, Work with source project → Initialize: opens the Initialize source project dialog (SourceInitializeDialog:Controls), which runs source_reconstruct with open true: it writes the metadata-free data/gamegen tree and opens the project root. It is the GUI's only reconstruction entry.
Welcome screen, Work with source project → Open: open_root with project true, which refuses a folder without data and gamegen, or one that is or lies below a link (not_project).

Export > Texture dithering (None, Ordered, Error diffusion) is the project's choice, saved in the project's hidden .zstudio/settings.json and passed to every export and check; source_dithering (an operation) reads or sets it, and source_status/source_export name it. Reads refuse a malformed settings file with invalid_argument; setting the dithering replaces a damaged file.
Pass destination to stage, re-parse and write every game file; replacing existing files needs overwrite (the GUI asks). Unsaved project edits must be resolved first.

Omit destination to build every output in memory and report failures and warnings without writing. Recognized but unimplemented world mutations report warnings in both this result and GUI Problems. Shared planning caps aggregate output inputs at 1,000,000 and pending/disk inventories at 50,000 files; imports refuse ambiguous glTF scene selection and malformed active world references.

Tools > Add model to world is shown unavailable for now (the Whole world toolbar has no Add model); source_world_add_model still adds a model to the active source world as one undoable source edit evaluated in memory. Save writes the sources and export alone creates game archives.

Source-project Blender checkout and update use the bundled RECOIL extension, complete source graphs, stable provenance and one shared undoable transaction. source_blender_extension supplies installation information. Completed exports are hash-verified and placement profiles in other owners remapped before acceptance. Explicit source/texture conflict consent cannot override invalid metadata. Only current version-two graph checkouts are listed; explicitly requested unsupported checkouts require a fresh checkout.

Tools > Create terrain chooses a glTF file in the project, then opens the Create terrain dialog (TerrainCreateDialog:Controls) for its meshes and recipe path; Create makes the recipe and the database marker as one undoable change (source_terrain_create with model, surfaces and recipe) and shows the recipe in Properties.
Tools > Paint polygon zones (P) engages the polygon zone tool in Paint on the shown source map, or switches an engaged tool to Paint: source_zone_tool with action engage and mode paint.
Tools > Erase polygon zones (E) engages the tool in Erase, or switches it to Erase: source_zone_tool with action engage and mode erase.

The Zones group's Edit zones toggle engages the tool (in its last mode and zone) or leaves it: source_zone_tool engage or exit. Engaged, the tool draws its own zone view and the overlays pause with their buttons disabled (scene_options highlight and faceOrientation return busy); leaving resumes them.
The Paint | Erase switch beside the engaged toggle sets the mode: source_zone_tool engage with mode.
The zone dropdown opens the zone picker (ZonePicker:Controls); source_zone_tool state lists the same zones with labels and polygon counts as placed in the world.
The tool banner's Exit leaves the tool, as Esc does: source_zone_tool exit.

Tools > Convert to editable terrain shows the plan (source_terrain_convert without apply), converts after confirmation as one undoable change and reports the altitude probe comparison (source_terrain_convert with apply). Ordinary recipes preserve converted runs in database encounter order. plan.recipe retains the first recipe; plan.recipes gives a bounded total/items/omitted summary. After acceptance, recipeListing identifies the existing read-only source_terrain command and replacement document for complete recipe pages. A bounded comparison reports complete=false and limitation when its work or index budget is exceeded, without failing the accepted conversion; plan reason previews disclose reasonTruncated.
Tools → Compare worlds… opens the one Compare worlds window; world_compare opens the same window and compares two files given by full path.

Edit mode, transform begin/confirm/cancel and pinned Properties use the same ai_path operations and draft/identity guards. Compiled worlds only for now: source worlds hide Edit path and ignore Tab; ai_path remains available.
Numeric transform input and world axis update the shared frozen-selection draft, preserving incomplete input until explicit confirmation or cancellation.

Shared Parachute flight/window selection, numeric or pointer draft, explicit confirm/cancel and actual animation-owner history/save. Compiled saves create a verified new copy; source saves retain project ownership. A selected unavailable flight exposes analysisRefusal while other candidates remain selectable. Samples/releases use offset/limit without query.

The back arrow left of the Whole world heading (Maps) returns to the source map picker after resolving drafts and save/discard/cancel. MCP closes the current document explicitly, requiring revision and discard consent for unsaved edits. Newer navigation supersedes pending map opening.

A source map's status-bar pane toggles: navigator (World tree), inspector (docked Properties) and tools (Diagnostics: the problems alone, read with zstudio_problems); the World tree and Properties are session-only, while Diagnostics shown/hidden and its height are remembered in the project's .zstudio/settings.json; never the compiled explorer's preferences.
The source map's Perspective chip menu runs the same projection, named view and framing actions as camera view/projection/frame.
The Flycam banner's Exit ends Fly like Escape; agents navigate with camera without capturing the user's physical mouse.
Collapse all is scene_tree collapse on the expanded rows (presentation only).

The outliner search box is scene_tree read with search: a flat list of matches with their parent paths (types optionally narrows it by the legend's categories). The info button's legend is static; rows carry category and pass in scene_tree read.
Choosing a flat match is scene_tree select on its row.
A row's Frame selection is scene_tree select on that row, then camera frame target selected.
A row's eye is scene_tree hide/show (view only, no source edit); scene_selection show_all shows everything again.

File > Open workspace… (Ctrl+O): open_root with project true, which refuses a folder that is not a source project (not_project, naming the missing data or gamegen folder), one that is or lies below a link, or one in an earlier source format.
